The '''Disciples of Twilight''' were a [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-[[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitive]] order based on [[Dyspeth]], a [[Moon/Legends|moon]] that was located in the shadows of an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. After the moon was colonized around [[900 BBY/Legends|900 BBY]] by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] who were seeking to break away from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], a [[Gender/Legends|female]] known only as "[[Twilight (individual)|Twilight]]," who was rumored to have been a former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and other Force-sensitive colonists founded the Disciples of Twilight. Members of the tradition became defenders and protectors of Dyspeth's citizens, although the group had no political or military influence. Dyspeth was discovered by Republic surveyors [[400 BBY/Legends|five hundred years]] later, and the Disciples of Twilight spread out into neighboring [[Star system/Legends|systems]]. Approximately [[137 ABY|one millennium]] after their creation, the organization had yet to choose a side in the [[Second Imperial Civil War|war]] among the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Darth Krayt|Krayt's]] [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Sith Empire]], deposed [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]]'s [[Empire-in-exile]], and the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant|remnants]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]].

==History==
Around [[900 BBY/Legends|900 BBY]], a group of [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists who sought to break away from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] migrated to a shadowy [[Moon/Legends|moon]] called [[Dyspeth]],<ref name="LE CG" /> located in the [[Varada sector/Legends|Varada sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="SW: TEA OC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> Shortly after the moon was colonized, a [[Gender/Legends|female]] known as "[[Twilight (individual)|Twilight]]," who was rumored to have been a former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], used her [[Force power/Legends|abilities]] with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to rally other [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] colonists in an attempt to adapt to the darkness of Dyspeth.<ref name="LE CG" />

After [[400 BBY/Legends|five hundred years]] of peace, a Republic team of surveyors located Dyspeth. The Dyspeth natives rejoined the Republic, albeit reluctantly, as reserved [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]] and traders. They began to spread to neighboring systems, but the people they met did not understand the motives of the Disciples. However, the Disciples were concerned with protecting the weak [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] from the misdeeds and injustices of the strong.<ref name="LE CG" />

By the year [[137 ABY]], during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], the Disciples of Twilight had yet to officially choose a side from among [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Darth Krayt|Krayt's]] [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]], the deposed [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]]'s [[Empire-in-exile]], and the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant|remnants]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. However, there were rumors from within the organization itself that the group was about to choose a side.<ref name="LE CG" />

==Philosophy and techniques==
After the individual known as "Twilight" formed the Disciples of Twilight, the members of the group sought to combine their efforts so they could adapt to Dysepth's dark environment. They eventually sought to defend the people of Dyspeth. The group believed in "shadowy justice"; when the tradition's members spread across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] after Dyspeth's discovery by the Republic, they sought to protect weaker sentients from the cruelty of the strong. While the Disciples of Twilight consisted primarily of Dyspeth natives, anyone who was Force-sensitive and agreed with the Disciples' beliefs was welcome to join.<ref name="LE CG" />

The [[Force Adept|Force adepts]] who were members of the Disciples of Twilight sought primarily to use the Force to bend light. After Dyspeth was located by the Republic, the members of the tradition that moved throughout the galaxy found that they were capable of using their Force powers to a greater extent, since most worlds were brighter than their own. The Disciples of Twilight shared powers comparable to the [[Fallanassi/Legends|Fallanassi]], who also possessed the ability of bending light. However, the group's members used other Force abilities that were unheard of anywhere else in the galaxy. Members used the Force to manipulate both light and darkness; the Disciples were capable of using the powers [[Force cloak|Cloak of Shadow]] and Shadow Armor to bend light so that they could render themselves invisible. They used the Force to [[Shadow Vision|gain low-light vision]] and to [[Revelation|locate]] enemies that concealed themselves. The adepts could also utilize the Force to [[Mind trick/Legends#Force illusion|create illusory phantoms]] around an enemy.<ref name="LE CG" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Disciples of Twilight were first introduced in the ''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]'', which was published by [[Wizards of the Coast]] for the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' and released on [[March 17]], [[2009]]. In the campaign guide, the group was featured as a new Force-using tradition.<ref name="LE CG" /> Dyspeth was later included in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'',<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and given a sector placement in its [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|online companion]].<ref name="SW: TEA OC" />
